workers.title: Fix Windows atomic publication temp filename length without weakening atomicity
workers.done_when: Both writeFileAtomic and writeFileAtomicDurable can safely publish valid near-max-length receipt paths (e.g. base filename length 243) without creating an over-255-character temporary basename; tmp stays inside destination directory, same-volume atomic replacement, unique O_EXCL CreateTemp, no overwrite of foreign evidence or weakening durable flush. Existing shorter paths work and existing writeFileAtomic failure/security semantics unchanged.
workers.instructions: ONLY MODIFY cmd/lock_windows.go. Current functions both call os.CreateTemp(dir, "."+filepath.Base(path)+".*.tmp"), so 243-char basename generates 258-byte final temp component and fails Windows NTFS even though target filename is valid. Add small deterministic helper e.g. atomicTempPattern(path string) whose ordinary short basename keeps the historical pattern; for long names (safe conservative threshold about 220 bytes) use SHA256 of filepath.Base(path) as a bounded anonymous temporary prefix (e.g. '.aw-' + first 16 hex + '-*.tmp'). Use the SAME helper in writeFileAtomic and writeFileAtomicDurable, no new filesystem/bridge or privilege. Never truncate or rewrite final destination basename or receipt contents. Use os.CreateTemp to generate random unique same-directory temp; keep existing replaceFileAtomicWindows, cleanup, durability and ACL. Do not change lockName, acquireLock, any other file, PLAN, installed binary, old receipt evidence. Small scoped source diff; no full Go suite.
